prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, converting small-molecule binding into the removal of chosen proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is the configuration with the broadest cross-member support (five top-three placements, two first places) and it meets my own test of a clear principle with generative potential. A bifunctional molecule forms a ternary complex whose cooperativity can be measured and tuned, and it hijacks the ubiquitin-proteasome machinery so that binding becomes removal, a different mechanism from inhibition. That has opened targets long considered undruggable and produced many clinical-stage compounds. Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept in 2001, and Ciulli supplied the VHL ligand chemistry and structural account of cooperativity that made degraders drug-like. This is a coherent three-person prize that can be explained to a broad audience in one sentence. I move B007 to first place after reading colleagues' arguments, since my opening first choice (B001, phase separation) has support from only two of us.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that PROTACs and molecular glues (cereblon: Handa, Ito, and the Gray and Sakamoto strands) may be two partly separate discoveries, and a three-name prize leaves out Handa and Ito, whose identification of cereblon explains thalidomide-type glues. There is also a maturity concern: no PROTAC is yet approved, so the medical payoff is promised rather than proven. Finally, the first PROTAC paper (2001) was a proof of concept with peptidic, cell-impermeable molecules, so the decisive drug-like chemistry is arguably later work, which makes the original discovery versus refinement distinction hard.

responses.point: Aili ranks B007 first and proposes Crews, Ciulli and Handa so that the prize covers both the PROTAC modality and the cereblon-based glue branch.
responses.response: I agree B007 deserves first place, but I qualify the Handa choice. Handa's identification of cereblon is a real discovery, yet it is a mechanism-of-action finding about an existing drug, not the design of a new modality. Including Handa and omitting Deshaies, who co-authored the 2001 founding paper, makes the citation harder to defend on priority. I would prefer to keep the citation to induced-proximity degradation and let the committee test whether glues belong inside it.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks B007 first as a game-changing modality and notes that timing is somewhat early, with no approved PROTAC, and that glues and PROTACs may be viewed as separate discoveries.
responses.response: I share Aqvist's concern about maturity, and I do not think it can be dismissed. My answer is that the chemical principle (ternary-complex formation and cooperativity) is independently confirmed by many groups and E3 ligases, so the science is mature even if the clinical endpoint is not. I would press Johan on whether a later year, after an approval, would be a better moment, because that is the real cost of acting now.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing (B052) first with a Liu, Komor and Gaudelli trio, arguing it turns a biological process into a controlled chemical reaction on DNA, and ranks B007 second as slightly early.
responses.response: I find the chemistry of base editing convincing, but I disagree on the trio. The evolved-deaminase work is Liu's intellectual program, and Komor and Gaudelli were the lead trainees, so a trio dilutes a clean story, and the 2020 CRISPR prize makes the committee ask what is new. I would keep B052 as my main alternative with Liu alone, but I would not rank it above degraders, since the generative potential of a new modality seems larger to me.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling (B029) first, with Buchwald and Hartwig, as a routinely used, three-decade-mature reaction that is not premature.
responses.response: I accept the impact and maturity argument, and I do not dispute that B029 is a robust candidate. My reservation as a physicist is what is fundamentally new: after the 2010 cross-coupling prize, C-N coupling reads as a very successful extension, and I would want Peter to say what conceptual step, beyond ligand generations, separates it from that precedent. If he can show it, I would support it as a strong alternative to B007.

responses.point: Sparr ranks phase separation (B001) first, as a reduction of cellular organisation to physical-chemical principles, with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen.
responses.response: I opened with B001 myself and still think the principle is the most elegant on the list, so I take Emma's case seriously. I now hold back because of what I flagged in my own opening: whether all reported condensates are true equilibrium phase separation, and how to split credit between the 2009 P-granule discovery and the multivalency framework. With only two of eight members ranking it first, I put B001 as an alternative rather than my preferred prize.

uncertainties: Whether the citation should cover molecular glues (Handa, Ito) alongside PROTACs, and whether a three-person limit can do that fairly.
Whether the lack of an approved PROTAC makes this year premature relative to a later year.
The exact priority split between the 2001 PROTAC concept and later drug-like VHL and cereblon degraders, which I am recalling from memory and have not verified.
Whether base editing (B052) is best treated as Liu alone given the 2020 CRISPR prize.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile; as a Lund physicist I have no direct tie to the protein-degradation candidates, and I note only that I would be judging chemical biology outside my own field.
